title: Near Sheldon village Wellington Memorial
location_name: Near Sheldon village, Peak District (Derbyshire / South Pennines)
memorial_type: Village memorial (Lancaster Bomber flypast conducted at 80th anniversary 2022)
narrative: Conducting a high-altitude pressurisation trial over Derbyshire, Wellington W5795 was lost on 12 July 1942 after a propeller sheared away at 35,000 feet and tore through the aircraft's cabin. Squadron Leader Colmore was piloting the development flight when the stricken bomber came down near Sheldon village in the Peak District. Five were killed: S/Ldr Cyril Colmore, P/O Kenneth Radford, Fl/Sgt Ronald Gillott, Fl/Sgt Arthur Smith DFM, and civilian test observer Clifford Abbott — who had joined the crew in a non-military capacity and was aged just 23.

crew.name: Cyril L.F. Colmore
crew.fate_detail: Killed when the pressurised cabin was breached at 32,500 feet after a propeller blade sheared off, causing catastrophic decompression.
crew.bio: Squadron Leader and pilot, aged 29. Led the classified high-altitude pressurisation test programme from A&AEE Boscombe Down.

crew.name: Kenneth Radford
crew.fate_detail: Killed in the catastrophic decompression and subsequent crash.
crew.bio: Pilot Officer serving with the RAFVR as second pilot, aged 27.

crew.name: Ronald P. Gillott
crew.fate_detail: Killed in the crash. The aircraft disintegrated, with wreckage spread between Dale Abbey and Ockbrook.
crew.bio: Flight Sergeant serving with the RAF, aged 22.

crew.name: Arthur J. Smith DFM
crew.fate_detail: Killed in the crash. His Distinguished Flying Medal indicates previous operational experience.
crew.bio: Flight Sergeant serving with the RAF, aged 23. Holder of the Distinguished Flying Medal, indicating exceptional operational service before his posting to the test programme.

crew.name: Clifford V. Abbott
crew.fate_detail: Killed in the crash. A civilian technical observer monitoring the pressurisation test.
crew.bio: Civilian test observer aged 23, attached to the experimental programme at Boscombe Down. One of the rare civilian casualties among these memorial records.

cause_of_loss: Propeller sheared off at 35,000ft, tore through pressurised cabin
memorial_details:
A polished grey granite tablet featuring the Royal Air Force badge was unveiled on 11 July 2004 in St Andrew's Churchyard, Stanley. The War Memorials Trust contributed towards the memorial costs. The inscription reads: "In Memory of The Crew of Wellington Mk VI W5795 Who Tragically Lost Their Lives On 12th July 1942 In A Crash In the Quarry Farm Area Of This Parish." Publicly accessible in the churchyard.

Memorial Unveiling (11th July 2004): A service was held to unveil the new memorial stone in St Andrew's Churchyard in Stanley Village, commemorating the 5 men lost in the Wellington Bomber W5795 crash.

Memorial Dedication (2004-07-11): Dedication of the memorial in St Andrew's Churchyard, Stanley, near Derby. This was the 72nd anniversary of the crash.

At 32,500 feet a propeller blade section sheared off, penetrating the cabin and causing decompression. Debris fell between Dale Abbey and Ockbrook.
